questions.question: What is the measure of central tendency that represents the middle value in a sorted dataset?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value when data is arranged in order, dividing it into two equal halves.

questions.question: Which measure shows how spread out the data values are from the mean?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation quantifies the amount of variation or dispersion in a dataset.

questions.question: What type of graph uses bars to show the frequency distribution of continuous data?
questions.explanation: Histograms display frequency distributions using adjacent bars for continuous data ranges.

questions.question: What is the most frequently occurring value in a dataset called?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often in a dataset.

questions.question: Which correlation coefficient indicates a perfect positive linear relationship?
questions.explanation: A correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a perfect positive linear relationship between variables.

questions.question: What percentage of data falls within one standard deviation of the mean in a normal distribution?
questions.explanation: In a normal distribution, approximately 68% of data falls within one standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question: Which statistical test is used to determine if there is a significant difference between two group means?
questions.explanation: A t-test compares the means of two groups to determine if they are statistically different.

questions.question: What is the square of the standard deviation called?
questions.explanation: Variance is the average of squared deviations from the mean and equals the square of standard deviation.

questions.question: Which value divides a dataset into four equal parts?
questions.explanation: Quartiles divide data into four equal parts, with Q1, Q2, and Q3 marking the divisions.

questions.question: What type of probability distribution is bell-shaped and symmetric?
questions.explanation: The normal distribution is a symmetric, bell-shaped curve centered around the mean.

questions.question: What is the mean of the dataset 2, 4, 6, 8, 10?
questions.explanation: The sum is 30 divided by 5 values, giving a mean of 6.

questions.question: What does a p-value less than 0.05 typically indicate?
options: The test failed to run correctly
The sample size is too small
questions.explanation: A p-value below 0.05 suggests the observed result is unlikely under the null hypothesis.

questions.question: Which value expresses how many standard deviations a data point is from the mean?
questions.explanation: A z-score standardizes values by measuring distance from the mean in standard deviations.

questions.question: What is the probability of an event that is certain to happen?
questions.explanation: Certain events have a probability of 1, while impossible events have a probability of 0.

questions.question: Which error occurs when a false null hypothesis is not rejected?
questions.explanation: A Type II error is a false negative, failing to detect an effect that actually exists.

questions.question: What is the term for the entire group that researchers want to study?
questions.explanation: The population is the complete group of interest, while a sample is a subset of it.

questions.question: Which plot best shows the relationship between two continuous variables?
questions.explanation: Scatter plots display paired values of two variables to reveal correlations and patterns.

questions.question: What is the interquartile range?
options: The middle value of the dataset
The difference between maximum and minimum
The difference between the third and first quartiles
questions.explanation: The IQR is Q3 minus Q1, covering the middle 50% of the data.

questions.question: If a distribution is skewed right, how do the mean and median typically compare?
options: The mean is less than the median
The mean is greater than the median
questions.explanation: Right-skewed data has high-value outliers that pull the mean above the median.

questions.question: What is the median of the dataset 3, 7, 9, 12, 15?
questions.explanation: The middle value of the five sorted values is 9.

questions.question: What does a confidence interval estimate?
options: The exact value of the parameter
A range likely to contain the population parameter
The total size of the dataset
questions.explanation: A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for a population parameter.

questions.question: Which continuous distribution assigns equal probability to all values within a range?
questions.explanation: The uniform distribution gives every value in an interval the same probability density.

questions.question: What is the range of possible values for a correlation coefficient?
questions.explanation: Correlation coefficients range from -1 (perfect negative) to +1 (perfect positive).

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The mean uses all values, so extreme outliers can shift it significantly.

questions.question: In hypothesis testing, what is the null hypothesis?
options: The statement of no effect or no difference
The research hypothesis the analyst wants to prove
The alternative explanation for the results
questions.explanation: The null hypothesis states there is no effect or difference, which tests attempt to reject.

questions.question: What does the standard error measure?
options: The variability of a sample statistic across repeated samples
The spread of raw data values
The difference between two group means
questions.explanation: Standard error quantifies how much a sample statistic like the mean varies between samples.

questions.question: An extreme outlier is added to a right-skewed dataset. What happens to the mean relative to the median?
options: The mean shifts toward the outlier more than the median
The median shifts more than the mean
questions.explanation: The mean uses every value's magnitude, so outliers pull it strongly; the median depends only on middle order positions.

questions.question: Why does sample variance divide by n-1 instead of n?
options: Bessel's correction yields an unbiased estimate of the population variance
Because samples are always smaller than 30
questions.explanation: Using the sample mean consumes one degree of freedom; dividing by n-1 (Bessel's correction) removes the downward bias.

questions.question: You compare mean blood pressure of two independent patient groups with n=25 each and unknown population variance. Which test is appropriate?
options: ANOVA F-test on three or more groups
questions.explanation: Comparing two group means with small samples and unknown variance calls for the two-sample (independent) t-test.

questions.question: A study reports p = 0.03. What does this mean?
options: There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
There is a 97% chance the result is real
If the null hypothesis were true, results at least this extreme would occur 3% of the time
questions.explanation: A p-value is the probability of observing data at least this extreme assuming the null hypothesis holds; it is not the probability the null is true.

questions.question: Which distribution models the number of successes in a fixed number of independent yes/no trials, such as heads in 10 coin flips?
questions.explanation: The binomial distribution counts successes in n independent Bernoulli trials with fixed success probability.
